context: The October 1 Binance PoR extraction, October 29 five-wallet XRP drain, CoinDesk's ETH-only PoR crosswalk, CoinGecko's September 30 liquidity report and XRP Insights' same-page ETF discrepancy create useful but non-synchronized evidence.
decisions: Treat the 91.42% Binance XRP reserve-wallet coverage result only as a conditional sensitivity scenario. Do not publish it as a current ratio unless the five XRPL source wallets are matched to the official XRP PoR address export and post-incident balances are measured.
Keep company funds and SAFU separate from the PoR reserve-wallet ratio. A wallet-level coverage stress is not a solvency finding.
Use CoinGecko's September 30 liquidity report only as historical venue-structure evidence. Require timestamped venue-level order books before admitting depth features.
Do not admit BibaMoney's page quote or depth until quote timestamp, venue data and depth table are captured and validated.
Do not admit XRP Insights aggregate ETF flows until header/detail discrepancies, GXRP exclusions, fund coverage, units, price basis and settlement dates are reconciled.

Do not issue a directional XRP forecast until synchronized point-in-time price, spot depth, derivatives, ETF and relevant macro/event features pass data-quality checks and fixed-horizon out-of-sample evaluation.
invariants: Every market observation retains source, retrieval time, source time and evidence classification.
Secondary PoR analyses are not treated as independent confirmation of the same Binance source data.
Public-chain analytics providers are independent analyses of common transactions, not independent transaction events.
Conditional stress calculations remain separate from confirmed balances.
Market features remain excluded until their freshness, venue coverage and timestamp rules pass.
No real-money trading; shadow/paper evaluation only after fixed-horizon forecasts are immutable and outcomes are recorded.
